job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Working Arrangements: On site

Closing Date For Applications: 27th November 2026

About the role:

The successful candidate will lead, coordinate, and drive the delivery of performance analysis support across all Academy age groups at Nottingham Forest FC. They will be responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the Academy analysis department, ensuring high-quality support is provided to players and staff throughout the development pathway.

The role will involve monitoring and tracking player development through the effective use of both objective and subjective performance data, helping to inform coaching practice and individual development plans.

In addition, the position holder will play a key role in upholding and embedding the Academy’s philosophy and methodology, supporting the wider vision of the Academy. Working closely with the Head of Player Development, Methodology and Innovation and Academy Coach Development Manager, they will contribute to the education and development of coaching staff while also actively participating in broader Academy management and strategic projects.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • To lead the support provision and requirements of the performance analysis function within the academy.

  • Oversee the analysis related to philosophy and methodology, aiding the academy vision.

  • Manage the day-to-day academy analysis operations ensuring effective processes to deliver actionable insights across all age groups.

  • Work in partnership with MDT teams to ensure high level reporting methods are delivered to players, coaches and key stakeholders across academy and loans.

  • Oversee individual analysis of Academy players using subjective and objective data to inform the Head of Academy and Academy Management Team.

  • Lead specific analysis projects related to the long-term development of Nottingham Forest Academy Analysis department.

  • Drive the club’s analytical products and processes to ensure the delivery of high-quality, actionable insights that support player development and performance outcomes.

  • Ensure effective professional development programme is implemented for both individual staff and analysis team.

  • Recruit permanent staff when the need arises in line with club protocols.

  • Manage and oversee the academy internship programme, supporting the recruitment, development, and day-to-day guidance of interns within the department.

  • Produce when required monthly, quarterly and yearly reports in line with our Academy strategy to update on progress met and achieved in relation to our performance analysis strategic pillar.

  • To create successful and professional relationships with players and staff whilst maintaining professional distance from playing staff at all times.

  • To act, at all times, in a manner appropriate to a representative of Nottingham Forest FC

  • All staff are responsible for the wellbeing and safeguarding of children and vulnerable adults on all Club sites. If you have a concern or witness a Safeguarding matter, you must report it to the department’s Designated Safeguarding Officer (DSO) or the Club’s Lead DSO or Senior Safeguarding Manager. If It’s an emergency, you are to call the relevant emergency service such as Police or CAMHS.

Skills, Experience and Knowledge:

  • Excellent understanding of football tactics and Talent Identification in players.

  • Excellent attention to detail and is very well organised and punctual

  • Able to communicate effectively at all levels and is fully computer literate.

  • Works effectively in a fast-paced environment; remains calm under pressure and is comfortable working to tight deadlines.

  • Prior experience managing kit and equipment for a sporting institution preferably within football (desirable)

  • Full knowledge and experience of all duties involved in a role of this nature.

  • Drive to achieve deadlines, organise and prioritise workload effectively, and continually review ways to improve efficiency and effectiveness

  • Demonstrate skills and attributes in a PA/administration capacity

  • Good verbal and written communication skills and be able to understand and explain matters arising in own area of work.

  • Excellent interpersonal skills, with people of all ages and backgrounds, able to maintain confidentiality, and act with tact and diplomacy

  • Willingness and flexibility to deal with urgent changes/ demands, whilst maintaining existing workload.

  • UEFA B license and educated in either Performance Analysis, Sports Science and/or coaching.

  • Excellent IT skills, including MS Office, intranets, web and Outlook

  • Experience in health and safety duties and responsibilities appropriate to the post (desirable)

  • Skill at handling difficult situations and confidential matters according to policy and procedures, referring to others where necessary/appropriate (desirable)

Forest For Everyone

At Nottingham Forest Football Club we are committed to creating an environment where differences are respected, individuality is celebrated, everyone feels valued, supported, and included. Our goal is to ensure every member of our team can be themselves, contribute fully, and reach their potential without barriers.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion and Mental Wellbeing

As an equal opportunities employer, we welcome applications from talented people of all backgrounds regardless of age, disability, gender identity or reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by law.

We continue to develop policies and practices that promote equality, diversity, inclusion and mental wellbeing across our workforce. To help us measure progress and hold ourselves accountable, we ask all applicants to provide accurate diversity information during the recruitment process.

Disability Confident Committed Employer

We are proud to be a Disability Confident Committed employer, taking positive steps to attract, recruit, and support disabled people. As part of this commitment, we work hard to ensure our recruitment processes are fair, inclusive, and accessible to everyone. We are committed to offering interviews for disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for a role and provide reasonable adjustments at every stage from the application process through to ongoing support in the workplace.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme. Please indicate this in your application form. The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check or an enhanced DBS check. The results of a DBS check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act in a proportionate manner when deciding whether or not to proceed with the appointment.

An FA Enhanced DBS disclosure is required for all relevant new appointments to the Club. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions or reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that may have been incurred. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed on a DBS disclosure if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements. Failure to satisfy the Club and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment.

Health and Safety

At Nottingham Forest Football Club, we are committed to ensuring a safe and healthy working environment for all employees. In accordance with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, you are required to take reasonable care for your own health and safety and that of others who may be affected by your actions or omissions at work. You must also cooperate with the Club's health and safety policies and procedures. Should you identify any health and safety concerns, please report them promptly to your manager or a member of the Health and Safety/Facilities team.

job.title: Partnerships Manager
job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 37.5 hours a week

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Partnerships

Reporting to: Director of Partnerships

Closing Date For Applications: 4th December 2026

About the Role:

The Partnerships Manager is responsible for the contractual delivery, management & renewal of Nottingham Forest’s commercial partners – alongside delivering any Premier League, FA, EFL activation. This includes the management, planning, reporting, activation and day-to-day relationships with the club’s Official Partners and league contractual obligations and across NFFC.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Working with the Director of Partnerships, with responsibility for management of partnership planning, contractual compliance, and activation within the commercial partnerships function.

  • Working closely with the partners and NFFC’s internal marcomms team to propose, develop and activate world class engaging campaigns and communications.

  • Responsibility for partnership measurement and evaluation, including up to date reports on delivery of contractual rights and ensuring over delivery of a partner’s key business and marketing objectives.

  • Responsibility for regular detailed partner reporting, working with Partnerships Insights Manager, utilising 3rd party TV, digital and media tools.

  • Day-to-day account management of the club’s major partners.

  • Management of partnership experiential rights, including player appearances.

  • Management of partner ticket and hospitality requests.

  • Updating partner matchday assets reporting internally & externally.

  • Responsibility for running matchday LED operations.

  • Ownership of partner matchday activations.

  • Working with the partnership sales department to propose potential activation campaigns for potential new partners.

  • Identifying areas of potential future incremental partner revenues, through cross selling, up selling or enhanced renewals with partners.

  • Work collaboratively with the Partnerships sales team to proactively identify new partners.

What are we looking for:

  • Experience in delivering world class marketing / partnership activations – ideally within sports at a rights owner or agency.

  • Passion for engaging with key commercial partners, with strong account management & relationship skills.

  • Ability to create, grow and maintain commercial relationships.

  • Experience in understanding a commercial partner’s marketing and business objectives and creating a plan that can be executed in order to deliver on those objectives.

  • A proactive mentality when it comes to problem solving.

Forest For Everyone

We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital / civil partnership status, pregnancy / maternity leave, race, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.

Disability Confident Committed Employer

We are a Disability Confident Committed employer.  We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions.  If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below.  The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check. The level of check required will depend on the requirements of the role. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that they are required to disclose for the level of check applicable to the role, in accordance with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (as amended) and the DBS filtering rules. The results of any check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act proportionately in deciding whether to proceed with the appointment. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements of the role. Failure to satisfy the Club, FA’s and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment, in accordance with the Club's disciplinary procedures

Health and Safety

Nottingham Forest is committed to maintaining a safe and healthy working environment for all employees, contractors, visitors, and guests. All employees are expected to comply with company health and safety policies, procedures and risk assessments, use equipment and PPE correctly and report any hazards, accidents and near misses. Appropriate training will be provided to ensure everyone understands their health and safety responsibilities.

job.title: Netball Pathway Physiotherapist
job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Engagement: Position offering variable hours on a flexible basis

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Netball

Reporting to: Netball Physiotherapist

Closing Date For Applications: 4th December 2026

Supporting Documents: Please attach relevant qualifications with your application.

About the Role:

Nottingham Forest Netball is seeking a qualified and experienced Physiotherapist to support the health, wellbeing and performance of our Netball Pathway athletes.

The role will involve providing physiotherapy cover at pathway matches and selected ad hoc training sessions, supporting the assessment, treatment and management of player injuries. The successful candidate will work closely with the Nottingham Forest Netball Head Physiotherapist to ensure a consistent, professional and athlete-centred approach to player care.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

Physiotherapy and Injury Management

  • Provide physiotherapy cover at designated Nottingham Forest Netball Pathway matches and ad hoc training sessions.

  • Assess, treat and manage player injuries, both acute and ongoing.

  • Provide pitch-side assessment and immediate injury management where required.

  • Support injury prevention strategies, rehabilitation programmes and player recovery.

  • Identify injuries requiring further medical assessment and ensure appropriate referral.

  • Support players in their safe and effective return to training and competition.

Communication and Collaboration

  • Work closely with the Head Physiotherapist to ensure continuity of care and consistent injury management.

  • Communicate player injuries, treatment plans and rehabilitation progress to the Head Physiotherapist in a timely and professional manner.

  • Liaise with pathway coaches and relevant staff, where appropriate, to support player welfare and performance.

  • Maintain accurate and confidential physiotherapy records.

Player Welfare and Professional Standards

  • Promote a positive, professional and athlete-centred environment.

  • Ensure all physiotherapy practice complies with relevant professional standards, safeguarding policies and medical protocols.

  • Maintain confidentiality and demonstrate appropriate professional boundaries when working with young athletes.

  • Contribute to the overall health, wellbeing and development of Nottingham Forest Netball Pathway players.

What are we looking for:

Essential

  • Recognised Physiotherapy degree or equivalent qualification.

  • Current registration with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC).

  • Recognised pitch-side trauma and emergency care qualification, such as Immediate Care in Sport (ICIS) or an equivalent qualification.

  • Experience in sports physiotherapy, injury assessment and management.

  • Ability to work independently and make sound clinical decisions in a sporting environment.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

  • A commitment to player welfare, safeguarding and professional standards.

Desirable

  • Postgraduate qualification in Sports Physiotherapy, such as an MSc in Sports and Exercise Physiotherapy, or equivalent recognised sports physiotherapy training.

  • Experience working within netball or another high-performance sporting environment.

  • Experience working with youth athletes and supporting long-term athlete development.

  • Experience in pitch-side emergency care and return-to-play management.

job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Department: Academy Sports Science and Medicine

Reporting to: Lead Academy Physical Performance Coach

Closing Date For Applications: 4th December 2026

Supporting Documents: Please attach relevant qualifications with your application.

About the Role:

This post is expected to optimise the availability and athletic development of Academy players through the provision, monitoring and passionate delivery of an evidence based physical development programme, in line with the Nottingham Forest Football Club Academy performance syllabus. As part of an MDT, work directly with the professional development phase (PDP) regarding all aspects of Sports Science and Performance on a day-to-day basis, to exceed the requirements of a Category 1 Academy as determined by EPPP. This role’s primary responsibility will be to lead the Performance support for either the U18 squad or the B Team, dependant on suitability of the successful candidate.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Provide professional and world leading physical performance support for all registered Academy players including individual programmes and long-term athletic development plans.

  • In association with the academy coaches, organise the weekly training plans and long-term programmes for academy age group players with a primary responsibility for a PDP team. This should include responsibility for players transitioning between the squads for training and matches.

  • Ensure Sport Science & S&C provision including session plans, gym sessions and testing are uploaded into the appropriate AMS within 24 hours.

  • Manage all pitch related physical performance in co-operation with other MDT team members for a PDP squad.

  • Ensure testing and monitoring practices are consistently implemented and evaluated to inform practice.

  • Assist in Talent Identification protocols and contribute to the trialling procedures and testing for potential academy players.

  • Educate staff to ensure the maintenance of age specific best practice including the provision of in-service training and appropriate CPD.

  • Collaborate across the Academy Performance department, aligning programming with synonymous athletic development methodologies.

  • Assist where appropriate other members of the performance and medical departments across all NFFC squads and teams, including rehabilitation support.

  • Work with the wider medical team to provide an integrated approach to performance enhancement regarding injury rehabilitation and return to training/play criteria.

  • In conjunction with the medical department, develop age-related prehab and appropriate rehab to minimise injury risk and maximise player availability.

  • Use appropriate databases to monitor and manage player loading, working closely with the multi-disciplinary team to individualise player plans.

  • To support with the management of the work placement students.

  • To contribute to player reviews and audits in order to assess performance and potential.

  • To provide physical performance support at home/away matches across a PDP squads.

  • To support with evidence-based departmental projects.

  • Any other appropriate duties as required by the Academy management team.

  • Responsible for both individual health & safety and that of those who you are responsible for.

  • Ensure the relationship with children and adults at risk is appropriate and language, behaviour and demeanour is suitable. The Company will expect you to undertake training to ensure an understanding of best practice in relation to children and/or adults at risk.

  • You will be responsible for the welfare of children in your care.

What are we looking for:

Essential:

  • BSc in Sports Science or equivalent.

  • UKSCA or equivalent.

  • Emergency First Aid Qualification

  • CASES accreditation

  • Ability to accurately measure and monitor essential physical components with elite youth athletes using a range of applied technologies.

  • Provide accurate and informative written and verbal reports to a range of key stakeholders.

  • Managing and developing databases to inform the above.

  • Coach youth athletes across a range of fundamental movements.

  • Exhibit age-appropriate communication techniques.

Desirable:

  • A postgraduate degree in sports science (or another relevant discipline).

  • Football coaching qualifications.

  • Relevant teaching qualification.

  • ISAK Accreditation

Forest For Everyone

We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital / civil partnership status, pregnancy / maternity leave, race, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.

Disability Confident Committed Employer

We are a Disability Confident Committed employer.  We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions.  If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below.  The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check. The level of check required will depend on the requirements of the role. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that they are required to disclose for the level of check applicable to the role, in accordance with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (as amended) and the DBS filtering rules. The results of any check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act proportionately in deciding whether to proceed with the appointment. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements of the role. Failure to satisfy the Club, FA’s and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment, in accordance with the Club's disciplinary procedures

Health and Safety

All employees are expected to comply with company health and safety policies, procedures and risk assessments, use equipment and PPE correctly and report any hazards, accidents and near misses. Appropriate training will be provided to ensure everyone understands their health and safety responsibilities.

job.title: Academy PDP Physiotherapist
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Academy Sports Science and Medical

Reporting to: Head of Academy Physiotherapy

Closing Date For Applications: 29th December 2026

Supporting Documents: Please attach relevant qualifications with your application.

About the Role:

This post is expected to involve contributing significantly to both the Medical and Performance departments to optimise the availability and enhance the long-term athletic development of Nottingham Forest Academy players through optimal service provision in the medical department. The role will require the individual to assist in the medical management, co-ordination and supervision of the of the PDP players, including all aspects of medical screening, injury assessment, diagnosis, management and prevention strategies in line with evidence-based practice. To assist the Head of Academy Physiotherapy in the day-to-day running of the medical department, working as a mentor for the junior staff.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • To primarily work with the B Team squad providing physiotherapy services.

  • To lead on the treatment and management of injuries sustained to players in the PDP squads, working closely with the performance staff to co-ordinate and deliver evidence and performance-based rehab programmes.

  • To standardise the management of injuries by assisting in the development and structure of injury rehabilitation protocols and philosophy.

  • To monitor the effectiveness of injury management principles through clinical injury audits and training availability.

  • To ensure effective, appropriate and thorough communication of injury updates are provided to the player, coaching staff and other relevant staff members.

  • To assist the Head of Academy Performance & Medical and Head of Academy Physiotherapy in the provision of physiotherapy services across all age groups and to help oversee the use of part time physiotherapists and sports therapists in their provision of medical care to all players in the Academy.

Injury Prevention:

  • To provide musculoskeletal screening/profiling for all Academy players and integrate this with the Club medical records.

  • To lead the musculoskeletal screening/profiling for PDP players and assist with the process for all Academy players and integrate this with the Club medical records.

  • To work alongside the performance staff to deliver individualised effective injury prevention strategies in both individual and group sessions.

  • To liaise effectively with the Academy coaching staff on a daily basis to keep them informed of players’ availability for Academy matches and training.

  • To work alongside the performance staff to deliver first class recovery and injury prevention strategies to all players both immediately after games and on recovery days.

  • To ensure all players are educated on the importance of recovery, health and athletic development.

Pre-Signing Medicals & Medical Consultations:

  • To assist co-ordinate the pre-signing medical assessments of all Academy players and trialist as required including the writing of formalised pre-signing medical reports.

  • To assist the Head of Academy Performance & Medical and Head of Academy Physiotherapy in escalating clinical cases for imaging and/or consultant referrals.

  • To accompany players to medical consultations at short notice either in this country or abroad. Ensuring best practice is always followed and ensuring the player receives optimal care and advice, providing clinical handovers pre and post appointment.

  • To assist the Academy Doctor in co-ordinating the cardiac screening for the PDP squads in line with FA regulations.

  • To manage the FA whereabouts schedule for the PDP squads and assist with the education of players regarding their anti-doping responsibilities.

Medical Provision at Matches/Training Sessions/Tours:

  • To provide physiotherapy match day cover for B Team games and assist other age groups when needed.

  • To assist in organisation and implementation of the medical provision for all training camps for the PDP squads as required.

  • To ensure all medical equipment and procedures are regularly reviewed and maintained at the training ground and at all training and match venues under the guidance of the Head of Academy Physiotherapy.

Management Responsibilities:

  • To take an active role in all medical meetings, MDT meetings and other planning meetings.

  • To take a mentoring role within the department, working as a mentor for junior physiotherapists and being pro-active with assisting CPD for the part time physiotherapists.

  • To assist in the production of an injury audit on a monthly and annual basis for the Academy and feedback to provide accountability for the department and actively seek to follow best practice.

  • To ensure appointments are made for consultations and appropriate travel arrangements made for all Academy players as required, ensuring the 1st Team Medical Department are notified in advance to manage the Club’s Health Partners insurance scheme.

CPD:

  • To assist with delivery and organisation of in-service training sessions in conjunction with the Head of Academy Performance & Medical and Head of Academy Physiotherapy, including the creation of a CPD department pathway to ensure the on-going development of knowledge and skills.

  • To take responsibility for continued professional development to ensure regular attendance of appropriate courses, conferences and keep an up-to-date file of CPD achievements, feeding back any relevant learning points to the department.

Professional Standards:

  • To produce daily reports of injured development players, ensuring all medical notes are up to date within 24 hours of treatment and in line with CSP core standards.

  • To ensure all medical documents are maintained in line with information governance principles.

  • To work with the Safeguarding team to highlight cases for attention through the appropriate channels as required and ensure all relevant training qualifications are maintained.

  • To always maintain a flexible approach to work, including the requirement to undertake other duties and responsibilities as required from time to time.

  • To keep confidential any information gained regarding the charity, Club and its personnel.

  • To ensure compliance with all relevant Club policies, including health and safety policies.

  • To always support Nottingham Forest FC in their aims and objectives.

  • To always represent Nottingham Forest FC in a professional manner.

What are we looking for:

Essential:

  • BSc (Hons) Physiotherapy or higher degree

  • Member of the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC)

  • Member of the Chartered Society of Physiotherapists (MCSP)

  • Valid ATMMiF Qualification

  • Indemnity through professional registration to £5 million liability

  • Minimum of 2 years post qualification experience

  • Experience of working within a multidisciplinary team

  • Sports Medicine environment preferably with younger athletes

  • Excellent clinical reasoning and manual therapy skills

  • Excellent problem solving and decision-making skills

  • Excellent range of clinical treatment skills an emphasis on rehabilitation

  • Excellence in the understanding and delivery of rehabilitation

  • Medicine from plinth to pitch

  • Management skills to manage a multidisciplinary group of part time practitioners within the Academy Medicine department

  • Set and maintain high standards of work performance and deliver quality consistently and effectively

  • A good understanding of the principles of human performance and how they relate to clinical sports medicine

  • A learning pathway showing the development of a strong evolving clinical paradigm in the field of Physiotherapy (minimum of 36 hours CPD annually to maintain professional registration)

  • Good knowledge of injury screening, diagnostics, manual therapy, injury prevention and recovery strategies

  • Ability to lead group sessions and deliver gym and pitch-based programmes to groups and individuals particularly to adolescents

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills that are clear, engaging and responsive to convey complex information

  • Exceptional organisational skills with the ability to manage competing demands and deadlines

  • Hold a full current up to date driving licence

  • Proactive and engaging style with a winning attitude and co-do approach. Flexible approach and attitude to working hours

  • Highest standards of professionalism and personal conduct – especially around the issue of confidentiality

  • Long term commitment to working within a multi-disciplinary medical team

Desirable:

  • Higher (MSc) Sports Medicine Degree

  • Sports Science Diploma/Degree

  • Playing experience to a high level

  • UKSCA/strength and conditioning qualifications

Forest For Everyone

We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.

We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.

We are a Disability Confident Committed employer.  We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions.  If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below.  The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check. The level of check required will depend on the requirements of the role. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that they are required to disclose for the level of check applicable to the role, in accordance with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (as amended) and the DBS filtering rules. The results of any check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act proportionately in deciding whether to proceed with the appointment. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements of the role. Failure to satisfy the Club, FA’s and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment, in accordance with the Club's disciplinary procedures

All employees are expected to comply with company health and safety policies, procedures and risk assessments, use equipment and PPE correctly and report any hazards, accidents and near misses. Appropriate training will be provided to ensure everyone understands their health and safety responsibilities.

job.title: Media Attendance Assistants
job.html_description:
We are looking for Media Attendance Assistants!

Job information
Division/Unit: Club Competitions Operations & Events
Contract type: maximum term
Start date: 01/03/2027
End date: 30/06/2027

Main goal

Your goal is to ensure the smooth journey of media stakeholders (press, photographers, video journalists, radio and TV non-rights holders) from their registration in the UEFA Media Channel, their media validation in the system, and eventually, accreditation and match booking requests to on-site attendance.

Key responsibilities

  • Overseeing the registration of bona fide Press, Photographers, Video Journalists, Radio & TV Non-Rights holders in the UEFA Media Portal
  • Ensuring an efficient accreditation and match booking media application process, in close liaison with UEFA ICT
  • Establishing documentation and standard operational processes that will be used by our counterparts, such as Press Officers, Onsite & Offsite staff, media representatives etc.
  • Coordinating the event-specific media stakeholders access needs with UEFA Accreditation and Access
  • Coordinating the media requests approval and rejection process with UEFA Communications as well as other internal stakeholders.
  • Answering the emails received from media representatives in a professional and client-centric approach
  • Assisting with the on-site delivery of media operations and services as required (Club and National Team Finals, Final Tournaments, Draws, etc.)
  • Applying the latest ICT developments to media services processes

Requirements

Experience:

  • Experience in event management where serving clients with high expectations is key and/or venue management in football or other sport
  • Good writing skills, including the ability to draft policies, guidelines and workflows

Education:

  • Bachelors' degree within the media environment, business management or sports/event management

Languages:

  • English / Advanced

Other requirements:

  • Knowledge of and interest in the sports media landscape in general, and particularly in football
  • Ability to provide outstanding results under pressure
  • Attention to details combined with the ability to see the big picture
  • The ability to work independently and reliably with precision and respecting confidentiality and multicultural concerns
  • A solution-oriented team player who is resilient, driven, amiable, energetic, diplomatic and charismatic with a positive outlook
  • Efficiency and the ability to keep track of numerous projects at once
  • Strong team spirit even in a high-pressure, changeable environment
  • Solid interpersonal skills with the ability to build a strong network
  • A creative and service-oriented mindset

job.title: Football Planning & Services Coordinator
job.html_description:
Job information
Division/Unit: Football / Football Planning & Services
Contract type: Fixed-term (maternity cover)
Location: Nyon (up to one day working from home per week)
Start date: 01.02.2027
End date: 31.07.2027
Application deadline: 25.11.2026

Main goal

Looking for an opportunity to experience UEFA from a different angle? This six-month role in the Football Planning & Services unit places you at the heart of projects that shape the future of UEFA competitions and finals. You will work and collaborate directly with experts from across UEFA, including legal, events, safety & security and competition management, and gain insight into planning, regulatory and operational dimensions.

Beyond the exciting projects, this is an excellent opportunity to develop valuable technical skills. The team actively uses tools such as Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Microsoft Forms, Power Apps, Python and Author-it, making this role ideal for someone eager to learn, grow and expand their professional toolkit in a fast-paced and collaborative environment.

Key responsibilities

  • Coordinating bidding projects for future finals and tournaments, assisting with requirements review, editing, publishing, communication and evaluation
  • Administrating the review process of UEFA regulations and competition manuals, working in close collaboration with the regulations managers and other stakeholders
  • Editing the content management system database in line with the ongoing review process and in collaboration with the relevant stakeholders
  • Formatting documents and content to ensure compliance with competition branding guidelines and corporate style standards
  • Collaborating with the lawyers responsible for the legal approval of such documents
  • Collaborating with English editors and translators to ensure the linguistic quality of the published documents
  • Ensuring consistency across UEFA bidding, competition regulations, competition manuals, technical regulations and, where possible, other official UEFA documents

Requirements

Experience:

  • Proven ability to work effectively within a team environment, supporting the coordination of document review, approval and publication processes while meeting tight deadlines

Languages:

  • English / Proficient

Other requirements:

  • Relocation to Switzerland/France is expected
  • Familiarity with automation and low-code tools (e.g. Python, Power Apps) would be an advantage – candidates should demonstrate either some practical experience in this area or a strong willingness to learn and develop these skills
  • Project coordination skills
  • Logical thinking skills


Want to stay updated on our latest job opportunities, events, and behind-the-scenes insights? Join us on LinkedIn.

job.title: Club Competitions Assistant
job.html_description:
Job information
Division/Unit: Football / Club Competition & Calendar
Contract type: Permanent
Location: Nyon (up to one day working from home per week)
Start date: 01.03.2027
Application deadline: 30.11.2026

Main goal

The Club Competitions Assistant will contribute to the efficient running of the Club Competition & Calendar unit by assisting the different domain managers with tasks related to their individual projects, analysis and reports, as well as cross-unit projects.

Key responsibilities

  • Supporting the two pillars of the unit (competition management & club services and events & projects) with their daily and season-related administrative tasks
  • Assisting with the administrative preparation of the competition entry process, access list, coefficients, calendars and regulations, as well as UEFA men’s club competition finals
  • Supporting all aspects of the preparation, implementation and delivery of club competition draws and calendars
  • Supporting the day-to-day management and monitoring of the competitions, ensuring the accurate and timely implementation of competition-related processes throughout the season
  • Assisting with the analysis of current competition-related processes and supporting their future planning, management and delivery
  • Contributing to the organisation and delivery of internal and external club competition meetings, events, working groups and workshops
  • Assisting with the administrative and logistical arrangements for UEFA Club Competitions Committee meetings
  • Assisting with the organisation and coordination of internal unit events and club competition-related travel
  • Gathering, validating and analysing competition data, preparing statistical overviews, drafting reports and creating presentations for internal and external stakeholders
  • Facilitating communication with internal and external stakeholders and ensuring an effective flow of information within the unit, across the division and with other departments
  • Contributing to the development of club competitions by preparing analyses of competition data, drafting reports and creating presentations

Requirements

Experience:

  • 1–3 years of internship or other work experience involving data management and analysis, ideally in an international or sports environment

Languages:

  • English / Proficient
  • Any other European languages would be an asset

Other requirements:

  • Relocation to Switzerland/France is expected
  • MS Office / Proficient
  • Administrative, planning and project-oriented competencies
  • Analytic thinking and approach
  • Strong knowledge of football, in particular club football
  • Good understanding of the football industry, particularly the competition organisation and development
  • Detail-oriented and highly organised, with a a high level of accuracy

Want to stay updated on our latest job opportunities, events, and behind-the-scenes insights? Join us on LinkedIn.

job.title: Event Workforce Assistant
job.html_description:
Job information
Division/Unit: UEFA Events SA / CEO Office
Contract type: Fixed-term ( 4 years)
Location: Nyon (WFH up to one day per week)
Start date: ASAP

Main goal

To further develop and manage a world-class event freelancer pool that enables the successful delivery of UEFA events through strategic workforce planning, compliant and efficient freelancer administration, and insightful reporting that supports operational excellence and informed management decisions.

Key responsibilities

  • Prepare, review and execute freelancer agreements across all UEFA competitions, ensuring accuracy and consistency
  • Ensure compliance with labour laws and internal policies, liaising with the UEFA legal department on freelancer contracts
  • Perform administrative tasks related to freelancers and their assignments, including daily communication and correspondence with freelancers
  • Process invoices from freelancers and follow up on payments in cooperation with the procurement and finance teams, and contribute to discussions on process enhancements and new operational developments
  • Follow up on budgets for different competitions in cooperation with the financial controllers
  • Onboard freelancers in the UEFA ICT environment and ensure that all required services and access rights are granted, in cooperation with the ICT team
  • Take an active role in workforce needs assessment activities by gathering project requests and consolidating them into a single source of information, while liaising with projects to clarify requirements when needed
  • Contribute to the preparation of a monthly workforce report for top management by aggregating data, performing data quality checks and presenting information in a clear and understandable way
  • Assist in implementing workforce analytics and reporting activities, including the development and maintenance of dashboards, KPIs and management reports
  • Support process improvement, automation and data management initiatives by optimising workforce-related processes, enhancing Power BI reporting solutions, ensuring data quality and integrity, and supporting the digital transformation of workforce operations

Requirements

Experience:

  • from 1 to 3 years in human resource management
  • from 1 to 3 years working in an international environment

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in relevant field

Languages:

  • Fluent in English

Other requirements:

  • Relocation to Switzerland/France is expected
  • Advanced MS Office (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Word)
  • Advanced CRM
  • Advanced SAP
  • Intermediate Tableau/Power BI
  • Ability to work in an international environment
  • Self-starter with proactive attitude towards tasks
  • Flexibility required to work in a dynamic environment
  • Strong attention to detail with a focus on data accuracy

Want to stay updated on our latest job opportunities, events, and behind-the-scenes insights? Join us on LinkedIn.

job.title: EURO Commercial Operations Coordinator
job.html_description:
Job information
Division/Unit: UEFA Events SA / Revenue Operations
Contract type: Max-term
Location: Nyon (WFH up to one day per week)
Start date: 01/02/2027
End date: 31/08/2028

Main goal

As part of the Commercial Operations team, the main goal of the Commercial Operations Coordinator is to provide operational support and ensure high professional standards in the delivery of on-site sponsorship rights for several elite national team tournaments, primarily UEFA EURO 2028, the 2027 UEFA Nations League finals and UEFA Under-21 EURO 2027.

For the national team competitions concerned:

  • Ensuring that UEFA’s commercial partners follow operational procedures and guidelines
  • Actively contributing to delivering commercial rights, including:
    • Partner guest-related rights
    • Partner activation rights and promotional opportunities
    • Sole and exclusive programmes and other individual rights
    • Partner on-site sales rights
    • Product supply management (value-in-kind services)
    • Partner commercial association exclusivity and UEFA rights protection

Key responsibilities

  • Supporting the operational management of the Commercial Operations team and providing general administrative support
  • Using selected modules in UEFA’s event management system (FAME), such as the accreditation module
  • Providing back-office support before and during events
  • Helping to produce key operational documents, prepare briefing materials and compile, filter and analyse reports
  • Taking part in briefings and debriefs
  • Helping the Commercial Operations team coordinate with internal and external stakeholders (other UEFA units, the commercial agent and UEFA's commercial partner)

Requirements

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree
  • Further studies in sports event management would be an asset
  • Project management qualifications are a plus

Experience:

  • from 1 to 3 years in event operations, ideally in sports marketing at an international level, including at venues

Languages:

  • Proficient in English

Other requirements:

- Relocation to Switzerland/France is expected

  • Proficiency in MS Office applications
  • Pragmatic and communicative approach
  • Ability to multitask in a fast-paced and deadline-driven environment
  • Team player
  • Good spoken and written communication skills

  • Willingness to travel
  • Good knowledge of sport in general and football in particular

job.title: Legal Operations Specialist
job.html_description: U.S. Soccer OverviewThe U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.Position Description As the first Legal Operations Specialist at U.S. Soccer, you will help our Legal department run core functions like document management, contract lifecycle management, legal billing and budgeting, technology and vendor management, and routing incoming correspondence. Just as important, you will partner with Legal leadership to improve operational efficiency, enable data-driven decision-making, and get more out of our technology, including AI-enabled tools.  This is a great opportunity to build the legal infrastructure of a rapidly growing department and make an impact across the organization. You won’t find a typical legal operations job here! You will join a collaborative team that values mentorship and high standards, supporting a national governing body during a period of tremendous growth and ambition. Expect a fast pace, a casual work environment, and a front-row seat to the work of growing soccer in America. The ideal candidate has legal operations experience, a passion for organization and efficiency, and excitement for building processes and systems. You stay calm in the face of chaos and aren’t afraid to challenge the status quo.  This full-time, non-exempt position is based at our national training center in Fayetteville, GA. We currently operate on a hybrid schedule, with in-office days every Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.Primary ResponsibilitiesDocument Management  Own our document management system and ensure that files are properly stored, named, and organized. Develop and maintain a cross-functional contract database. Receive and route physical legal mail. Process Management & Improvement Improve and streamline legal department processes by identifying, assessing, and implementing new processes, and leading change management to drive adoption. Document processes, create workflow diagrams and clear visuals to support operational improvements and stakeholder understanding. Assist with building and scaling a system for managing legal requests across the company. Ensure intake, routing, prioritization, and tracking are seamless and visible. Work closely with other departments to ensure legal processes align with how the business operates.  Own and maintain legal knowledge spaces (e.g., on the company’s intranet) by keeping them organized, current, and easy to navigate.  Legal Billing & Budget Management Oversee the e-billing and matter management system, including onboarding vendors, fielding questions, and collecting accruals. Develop and maintain relationships with law firm billing departments, and review outside counsel invoices for compliance with billing guidelines. Assist with managing the department budget. Technology & Vendor Management Partner with our paralegal to own the legal tech stack – managing tools like Ironclad, DocuSign, etc.  Leverage AI to automate workflows and reduce manual work.  Research, evaluate, and recommend emerging technologies, including AI-enabled tools, to improve efficiency.  Reporting & Analytics Assist Legal leaders in developing and implementing metrics and benchmarking to measure and report on team performance. Oversee the creation of regular, executive-level performance reports and presentations on legal department efficiencies, achievements, and value creation. General Responsibilities Operate with a strong bias for action, proactively identifying opportunities, driving initiatives forward independently, and exercising sound judgment on when to escalate things. Proactively engage with the legal operations community, industry forums, and vendor networks to identify emerging best practices and recommend improvements to our legal operations function. You may be asked to take on other tasks as assigned by Legal leadership.

Ensure intake, routing, prioritization, and tracking are seamless and visible. Work closely with other departments to ensure legal processes align with how the business operates.  Own and maintain legal knowledge spaces (e.g., on the company’s intranet) by keeping them organized, current, and easy to navigate.  Legal Billing & Budget Management Oversee the e-billing and matter management system, including onboarding vendors, fielding questions, and collecting accruals. Develop and maintain relationships with law firm billing departments, and review outside counsel invoices for compliance with billing guidelines. Assist with managing the department budget. Technology & Vendor Management Partner with our paralegal to own the legal tech stack – managing tools like Ironclad, DocuSign, etc.  Leverage AI to automate workflows and reduce manual work.  Research, evaluate, and recommend emerging technologies, including AI-enabled tools, to improve efficiency.  Reporting & Analytics Assist Legal leaders in developing and implementing metrics and benchmarking to measure and report on team performance. Oversee the creation of regular, executive-level performance reports and presentations on legal department efficiencies, achievements, and value creation. General Responsibilities Operate with a strong bias for action, proactively identifying opportunities, driving initiatives forward independently, and exercising sound judgment on when to escalate things. Proactively engage with the legal operations community, industry forums, and vendor networks to identify emerging best practices and recommend improvements to our legal operations function. You may be asked to take on other tasks as assigned by Legal leadership.

job.title: Pro License Educator
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is looking for a Pro License Coach Educator to facilitate the U.S. Soccer Pro License and support the continued development of coaches working at the highest levels of the professional game. 


The ideal candidate combines significant experience in the professional game with expertise in player development and coach education. They understand the realities and demands of professional coaching and can create meaningful learning experiences that connect course learning with each student’s professional environment.


Working with the Pro License Technical Lead, this role will guide students through course learning, application in their club environments, feedback, reflection, and assessment. The Pro License Coach Educator will report to the Senior Director of Coaching Education and work closely with the Coach Education technical and operational staff, the Sporting Department, professional leagues and clubs, Coach Educators, mentors, and specialist contributors.


The role will also work closely with the Head of Continuous Professional Development to create and facilitate development opportunities that respond to the evolving needs of Pro-level coaches and the professional game


Primary Responsibilities

  

Pro License Course

  • Facilitate the Pro License curriculum across in-person and virtual learning experiences, mentoring, club visits, and application within students’ professional environments
  • Contribute to the continued improvement of the Pro License through insights from students, course delivery, research, and developments within the professional game

Student Learning & Development

  • Understand each student’s context, experience, strengths, and development needs
  • Build effective relationships and facilitate dialogue, reflection, and reality-based learning grounded in professional practices
  • Help students identify a development focus, apply learning in their club environment, gather evidence of their practice, and reflect on what they learn

Assessment & Mentoring

  • Observe professional practice, provide meaningful feedback, and support students and mentors
  • Document evidence of student learning and contribute to assessment and reassessment decisions in line with Pro License standards and processes
  • Contribute to consistency in assessment and Coach Educator practice across the Pro License

Player Development and the Professional Game

  • Bring current expertise in player development and the men’s and women’s professional game to connect individual and team development, game models, coaching processes, and performance demands
  • Adapt learning to the distinct player development, performance, and working environments across the men’s and women’s professional game
  • Ensure learning remains relevant to the evolving realities of professional soccer in the United States

Research, Innovation, and Continuous Professional Development

  • Stay current with research, innovation, emerging practice, and developments within the professional game
  • In collaboration with the Head of Continuous Professional Development, translate relevant research and emerging practice into meaningful development opportunities for Pro-level coaches   

Professional Partnerships

  • Build productive relationships across U.S. Soccer and with MLS, NWSL, USL, professional clubs, technical leaders, researchers, and specialists
  • Use these relationships to strengthen learning, connect education with the professional game, and provide students with access to relevant expertise and professional environments

Professional Standards

  • Model the professional standards expected of U.S. Soccer Coach Educators, including safeguarding, inclusion, confidentiality, professional integrity, and responsible handling of student and club information

Requirements


Qualifications

  • Coaching Certification: U.S. Soccer Pro License or other confederation Pro License required
  • Education:  Bachelor’s degree in Coaching, Coach Education, Sport Science, High-Performance Coaching, Education, Adult Learning, or a related field preferred
  • Experience: Significant experience in professional coaching, technical leadership, player development, coach education, or high-performance environments.
  • Travel: Ability to travel nationally, conduct club visits, and work evenings and weekends when required by course delivery and the professional-game calendar.
  • Language: English required; Spanish proficiency is a plus
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States


Candidate Profile

We are looking for an experienced professional who can operate credibly across professional soccer and coach education. The successful candidate will bring:

  • Significant experience within professional soccer and a strong understanding of the realities and demands facing coaches, players, staff, and clubs
  • Deep expertise in player development and the ability to connect individual player development with team development, the game model, training, competition, and the wider performance environment
  • Current understanding of the men’s and women’s professional game in the United States, including MLS, NWSL, USL, their clubs, player pathways, competitive environments, and evolving coaching demands
  • Strong understanding of the women’s professional game and considerations relevant to female player development
  • Experience as a Coach Educator, including facilitating adult learning, mentoring coaches, observing professional practice, providing feedback, and contributing to assessment
  • Sound judgment in evaluating professional practice against defined standards, using evidence to support fair and consistent assessment
  • Ability to build trust and engage experienced professional coaches in meaningful dialogue, reflection, and learning
  • Curiosity about the game and a commitment to research, innovation, and continuous learning
  • Ability to translate research, emerging practice, and developments in the professional game into relevant learning experiences for coaches
  • Strong relationship-building and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across U.S. Soccer and with professional leagues, clubs, technical leaders, researchers, and specialists


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Case Administrator, Safeguarding
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is dedicated to safeguarding through creating a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment for everyone involved in the game—especially players, coaches, referees, and volunteers. We work proactively to keep individuals with harmful intentions out of the soccer community through programs like Safe Soccer Clearance. We promote awareness and healthy behaviors across the sport to build a culture of well-being and safety. If harm or abuse occurs, we work to ensure it is identified, reported, and addressed quickly, appropriately, and with care for the survivor. Our goal is to maintain a system of policies, practices, and values that protect all participants—especially children and vulnerable individuals—from harm and abuse.


We are looking for a compassionate, detail-oriented, self-starter to join the small team of reporting and response professionals in our Safeguarding group as Case Administrator. The team processes a high volume of safeguarding-related reports each year, oftentimes directing reports to the U.S. Center for SafeSport, one of U.S. Soccer’s organization members, and/or law enforcement. The team also assists the organization with the administration of its Safe Soccer Clearance program by helping individuals appeal adverse participation or membership decisions made as a result of flags on their background screening. 


The Case Administrator plays a vital role in addressing complex and often emotionally challenging issues. The ideal candidate will bring not only a strong sense of purpose and commitment to the work, but also emotional intelligence, empathy, and resilience. Comfort with sensitive subject matter and the ability to engage thoughtfully and respectfully with diverse perspectives are essential for success in this role.


This is position reports to our Manager, Safeguarding Administration and is based at our National Training Center in Fayetteville, GA. The NTC offers a hybrid works schedule, with employees reporting to the office in person on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday of each week. 


Primary Responsibilities


Background Screening Appeal Administration

  • Identify flagged screening reports and prepare them for review by an independent review panel
  • Identify screening reports that must be reported to the Center for SafeSport and/or law enforcement, and ensure that the organization’s mandatory reporting obligations are fulfilled
  • In consultation with the Manager, Safeguarding Administration and the SVP of Compliance & Safeguarding, communicate with U.S. Soccer’s background screening vendor on questions involving the organization’s flag matrix
  • Compile information from appellants to present to independent appeals panels, and coordinate the scheduling of live hearings
  • Educate appellants and organization members on the appeals process
  • Develop and maintain electronic case records

SafeSport Report Processing

  • Review reports received through U.S. Soccer’s reporting mechanisms
  • Refer reports to the U.S. Center for SafeSport, relevant organization members, and/or law enforcement where necessary and appropriate
  • Support organization members in navigating their reporting requirements and educate organization members on their response and resolution options
  • Respond to the Center for SafeSport’s information requests and communicate the Center for SafeSport’s notices and decisions to U.S. Soccer members
  • Update and maintain U.S. Soccer’s risk management list and the U.S. Soccer Learning Center’s disciplinary list
  • Develop and maintain electronic case records

U.S. Soccer recognizes that this role involves abuse reporting and that this is topic is upsetting and emotionally demanding. We are committed to supporting our Safeguarding team’s well-being. We foster a culture of openness and care, encouraging employees to speak up when they need support. 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university is preferred, but commensurate experience will be considered. A degree in a human services-related field is preferred, but not required
  • 3-5 years of experience with case management (e.g. child and family services, insurance claims, protective services, social services, non-clinical case management) is a plus
  • Experience with safeguarding preferred, but not required
  • Experience working with case management software preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate with empathy, compassion, and emotional intelligence across a diverse range of individuals and stakeholders
  • Proven ability to navigate sensitive situations with tact, active listening, and thoughtful response
  • Ability to stay focused, juggle multiple things at once, and know what to prioritize
  • Displays a service-oriented mentality, with the ability to get things done on time, and respond to stakeholders’ needs with a sense of urgency
  • Ability to work independently but collaboratively with other members of the Safeguarding team
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality of sensitive information 
  • Strong interpersonal skills, a positive attitude and the ability to communicate clearly and concisely both verbally and in writing
  • General knowledge of soccer
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.
