job.title: Senior Manager, Donor Direct Marketing
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


Reporting to the Director, Annual Fund, the Senior Manager, Donor Direct Marketing leads the strategy, development, and execution of U.S. Soccer's Mass donor marketing and communications function.


This seat owns the mass audience segment of the donor file, meaning constituents making single gifts outside of a membership, from first gift through the mid-level entry point. It carries a revenue and donor target against that audience and grows it through an agency of record supplying direct mail, email, and paid digital. U.S. Soccer owns the thinking. The agency owns the making. This seat holds that line.


The work is to integrate a channel mix, build an entry ladder, and put a second gift behind every acquisition, and to establish the operating model, campaign calendar, attribution standard, and measurement discipline the program runs on. The Senior Manager also serves as Advancement's liaison to centralized Marketing & Communications.


Primary Responsibilities


The Mass Audience Program

  • Own the mass audience segment of the donor file and the FY27 revenue and donor targets committed against it, from acquisition and second gift through retention, reactivation, upgrade, and the transition into mid-level giving.
  • Design and execute the second gift program, build monthly recurring giving into every touch rather than running it as a standalone campaign, and lead retention and reactivation, moving reactivation from direct mail to email and paid digital.

Growth, Testing, and Channel Development

  • Build and run a rolling test plan across creative, offer, ask string, segment, and timing, each with a stated hypothesis and a read date, and move proven results into the standing program.
  • Expand digital reach and revenue through paid social, search, display, and connected TV, lookalike and retargeting audiences built off the donor file, and owned channels including the U.S. Soccer app, match day, and email.
  • Evaluate and launch new channels, platforms, and partners, including list and audience partnerships, digital fundraising platforms, and SMS, piloting each against a defined budget, target cost per donor, and decision point. Lead the first-year digital build: a low dollar acquisition pilot against the post World Cup file, and a triggered welcome and second gift series.

The Agency Program

  • Manage the agency of record relationship day to day, including the brief, creative review, calendar commitments, and accountability to committed revenue projections. Maintain the division of responsibility that keeps strategy, audience, offer architecture, segmentation, source coding, and copy approval in house while the agency delivers modeling, production, deployment, media buying, and matchback.
  • Manage media investment within the approved budget, including target cost per donor acquired, reallocation between channels, and the decision to discontinue an underperforming line. Lead the transition to the go-forward partner and recommend the ongoing mix of internal staff, agency scope, and shared Federation services.

The Campaign Calendar

  • Own the campaign calendar across the fiscal year and coordinate timing across the Federation so that appeals, the Fan Experience communications queue, and the membership renewal cycle do not collide.

Attribution and Measurement

  • Own attribution for the mass audience. Enforce the source coding standard on every touch, internal and agency, reproduce the agency matchback internally so that every campaign is read twice, and report cost per donor acquired, twelve-month value by acquisition source, response rate, average gift, and second gift rate.

Donor Communications and Storytelling

  • Own the message architecture across the donor journey, covering what each segment receives between asks as well as during them, and advance appeal messaging from a benefits framing to an impact framing themed against U.S. Soccer's philanthropic pillars.
  • Build the impact story intake process, drawing from Soccer Forward and the stewardship pipeline with rights and release status attached to each item, and own stewardship, acknowledgment, and impact reporting for the mass audience.

Cross-functional Partnership

  • Serve as Advancement's liaison to centralized Marketing & Communications on channel access, calendar position, brand approval, audience data, and message alignment.
  • Partner with Stewardship & Engagement, Advancement Services, Memberships, Major Gifts, and Principal Gifts on segmentation, gift attribution, and lifecycle transitions into and out of the mass audience, and with Corporate Partnerships on the match or challenge behind each pillar campaign.
  • Collaborate with Product, Digital, and Fan Experience on recurring giving capability, donation form performance, and the tracking required to attribute a gift to a specific appeal.
  • Support overall goals of the Advancement department.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in nonprofit direct response fundraising, integrated marketing, donor engagement, digital marketing, communications, advancement, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated success developing and executing multi-channel direct response programs across direct mail, email, and paid digital that drive donor acquisition, retention, and revenue growth.
  • Experience managing an agency or vendor relationship, including briefing creative, holding a partner to a campaign calendar, and evaluating performance against committed projections.
  • Experience building or significantly expanding donor marketing, fundraising communications, or audience engagement programs.
  • Experience designing and reading a testing program, including hypothesis, sample, and result, and carrying a proven test into the standing program.
  • Experience evaluating and launching new acquisition channels, platforms, or audience partnerships against a target cost per donor.
  • Working knowledge of fundraising analytics, including cost per donor acquired, donor value by acquisition source, response rate, and matchback methodology.
  • Strong understanding of donor lifecycle marketing, audience segmentation, source coding and attribution, and CRM-driven communications.
  • Proven ability to think strategically while leading complex campaigns from concept through execution.
  • Experience collaborating across fundraising, marketing, technology, digital, and communications teams within a complex organization.

Position Description
Reporting to the Director, Annual Fund, the Senior Manager, Donor Direct Marketing leads the strategy, development, and execution of U.S. Soccer's Mass donor marketing and communications function.
This seat owns the mass audience segment of the donor file, meaning constituents making single gifts outside of a membership, from first gift through the mid-level entry point. It carries a revenue and donor target against that audience and grows it through an agency of record supplying direct mail, email, and paid digital. U.S. Soccer owns the thinking. The agency owns the making. This seat holds that line.
The work is to integrate a channel mix, build an entry ladder, and put a second gift behind every acquisition, and to establish the operating model, campaign calendar, attribution standard, and measurement discipline the program runs on. The Senior Manager also serves as Advancement's liaison to centralized Marketing & Communications.
Primary Responsibilities
The Mass Audience Program
- Own the mass audience segment of the donor file and the FY27 revenue and donor targets committed against it, from acquisition and second gift through retention, reactivation, upgrade, and the transition into mid-level giving. - Design and execute the second gift program, build monthly recurring giving into every touch rather than running it as a standalone campaign, and lead retention and reactivation, moving reactivation from direct mail to email and paid digital.
Growth, Testing, and Channel Development
- Build and run a rolling test plan across creative, offer, ask string, segment, and timing, each with a stated hypothesis and a read date, and move proven results into the standing program. - Expand digital reach and revenue through paid social, search, display, and connected TV, lookalike and retargeting audiences built off the donor file, and owned channels including the U.S. Soccer app, match day, and email. - Evaluate and launch new channels, platforms, and partners, including list and audience partnerships, digital fundraising platforms, and SMS, piloting each against a defined budget, target cost per donor, and decision point. Lead the first-year digital build: a low dollar acquisition pilot against the post World Cup file, and a triggered welcome and second gift series.
The Agency Program
- Manage the agency of record relationship day to day, including the brief, creative review, calendar commitments, and accountability to committed revenue projections. Maintain the division of responsibility that keeps strategy, audience, offer architecture, segmentation, source coding, and copy approval in house while the agency delivers modeling, production, deployment, media buying, and matchback. - Manage media investment within the approved budget, including target cost per donor acquired, reallocation between channels, and the decision to discontinue an underperforming line. Lead the transition to the go-forward partner and recommend the ongoing mix of internal staff, agency scope, and shared Federation services.
The Campaign Calendar
- Own the campaign calendar across the fiscal year and coordinate timing across the Federation so that appeals, the Fan Experience communications queue, and the membership renewal cycle do not collide.
Attribution and Measurement
- Own attribution for the mass audience. Enforce the source coding standard on every touch, internal and agency, reproduce the agency matchback internally so that every campaign is read twice, and report cost per donor acquired, twelve-month value by acquisition source, response rate, average gift, and second gift rate.
Donor Communications and Storytelling
- Own the message architecture across the donor journey, covering what each segment receives between asks as well as during them, and advance appeal messaging from a benefits framing to an impact framing themed against U.S. Soccer's philanthropic pillars. - Build the impact story intake process, drawing from Soccer Forward and the stewardship pipeline with rights and release status attached to each item, and own stewardship, acknowledgment, and impact reporting for the mass audience.
Cross-functional Partnership
- Serve as Advancement's liaison to centralized Marketing & Communications on channel access, calendar position, brand approval, audience data, and message alignment. - Partner with Stewardship & Engagement, Advancement Services, Memberships, Major Gifts, and Principal Gifts on segmentation, gift attribution, and lifecycle transitions into and out of the mass audience, and with Corporate Partnerships on the match or challenge behind each pillar campaign. - Collaborate with Product, Digital, and Fan Experience on recurring giving capability, donation form performance, and the tracking required to attribute a gift to a specific appeal. - Support overall goals of the Advancement department. - Perform other duties as assigned.
Requirements
Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree required. - 5+ years of progressive experience in nonprofit direct response fundraising, integrated marketing, donor engagement, digital marketing, communications, advancement, or related fields. - Demonstrated success developing and executing multi-channel direct response programs across direct mail, email, and paid digital that drive donor acquisition, retention, and revenue growth. - Experience managing an agency or vendor relationship, including briefing creative, holding a partner to a campaign calendar, and evaluating performance against committed projections. - Experience building or significantly expanding donor marketing, fundraising communications, or audience engagement programs. - Experience designing and reading a testing program, including hypothesis, sample, and result, and carrying a proven test into the standing program. - Experience evaluating and launching new acquisition channels, platforms, or audience partnerships against a target cost per donor. - Working knowledge of fundraising analytics, including cost per donor acquired, donor value by acquisition source, response rate, and matchback methodology. - Strong understanding of donor lifecycle marketing, audience segmentation, source coding and attribution, and CRM-driven communications. - Proven ability to think strategically while leading complex campaigns from concept through execution. - Experience collaborating across fundraising, marketing, technology, digital, and communications teams within a complex organization. - Exceptional communication, storytelling, project management, and relationship-building skills with the ability to influence stakeholders across all levels of an organization. - Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook). - Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments. - Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission. - Ability to work evenings, weekends, and travel as needed.
Desired Qualifications
- General knowledge of soccer. - Experience supervising staff, agency teams, or cross-functional project teams. - Experience utilizing Salesforce, marketing automation platforms, email marketing systems, or comparable CRM and digital marketing technologies.

Position Description


Reporting to the Director, Annual Fund, the Campaign Sr Coordinator owns the campaign calendar and the production behind it. This is a project management role with fundraising experience, accountable for moving every appeal, stewardship touch, and information moment from brief to drop, on schedule and correctly coded.


The calendar runs the full fiscal year and stays live rather than being rebuilt each quarter. Story intake sits with this seat as well, as a standing pull against programs across the Federation, banked with rights status attached so that a campaign brief begins from cleared evidence.


Primary Responsibilities


The Campaign Calendar 

  • Own the fiscal year campaign calendar covering every appeal, stewardship touch, and information moment, visible to every team that plans against it.
  • Confirm dates with Fan Experience, Membership, and Stewardship before they are committed.

Campaign Production

  • Run production from brief to drop across direct mail, email, and paid digital: creative routing, internal and legal approvals, proofs, data pulls, list and seed delivery, and drop dates.
  • Maintain the campaign brief as the single source of truth for audience, offer, ask string, timing, and creative direction, with a defined audience before work begins.
  • Run quality control before release, including proofing, link and donation path testing, personalization, and suppression verification, and maintain version control and archival so every campaign has a retrievable record of what dropped, to whom, and when.

Agency and Vendor Coordination

  • Hold the agency production schedule against ours and manage print, lettershop, data, and fulfillment vendors on timelines, postal drop windows, and delivery confirmation, escalating slipped dates before they affect a drop.

Story Intake and Content Operations

  • Build and run a standing story intake against Federation programs, maintaining a library of impact stories with rights, release, and usage status attached to each item.

Campaign Setup and Coding

  • Issue campaign IDs, source codes, and coded URLs against the U.S. Soccer source coding standard for every touch, internal and agency.
  • Set up campaigns in Salesforce and the email platform, including audience selections, tracking, and the records the program is reported from.

Cross-functional Partnership

  • Partner with Advancement Services on data pulls, segmentation delivery, suppression, and gift processing timelines.
  • Coordinate with Marketing & Communications, Fan Experience, Digital, and Product on channel access, calendar position, and brand approvals.
  • Support overall goals of the Advancement department.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications 

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • 3+ years of project management or campaign production experience in nonprofit fundraising, direct response marketing, agency account management, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multi-channel campaign production from brief through delivery, across direct mail, email, and digital.
  • Experience building and maintaining a production calendar across multiple concurrent campaigns and competing stakeholders.
  • Working knowledge of direct mail production, including backward planning from the in-home date, proofing cycles, data and list processes, and postal timelines.
  • Experience coordinating agency or vendor deliverables against a schedule, including escalating slipped dates before they affect a drop.
  • Meticulous attention to detail, particularly in proofing, quality control, and version control.
  • Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to hold peers and partners to a deadline without direct authority over them.
  • Comfort documenting process and building a system where none exists.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Ability to work evenings, weekends, and travel as needed.


Desired Qualifications

  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Experience utilizing Salesforce, marketing automation platforms, email marketing systems, or comparable CRM and digital marketing technologies.
  • Experience with source coding, campaign attribution, or marketing operations.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Corporate Development team leads U.S. Soccer’s inorganic growth initiatives, advancing strategic priorities and creating long-term value for the Federation. Our work includes mergers and acquisitions, joint ventures, strategic investments / partnerships, integration planning and real estate development. We partner with teams across U.S. Soccer, including Finance, Strategy, and Legal to deliver on our projects. 


The Senior Manager, Transaction Execution is a core member of the Corporate Development team and will conduct due diligence, perform financial analyses, manage project workstreams, coordinate across Finance, Legal, HR, IT, Communications, and program teams, and prepare strategic discussion materials to drive key strategic transactions and initiatives at US Soccer. This role supports multiple concurrent transactions and serves as the day-to-day execution lead on each. 


Primary Responsibilities

  • Support the identification, evaluation, structuring, and execution of mergers, acquisitions, managed service agreements (MSAs), joint ventures, strategic investments, and partnerships. 
  • Build and maintain financial models and analyses, including transaction economics, funding and pro forma analyses, and scenario and sensitivity analyses. 
  • Run due diligence end to end across internal teams and external advisors, including managing data rooms, information requests, and issue tracking. 
  • Lead cross-functional working groups, gathering input from each function on how their areas will change and keeping them aligned through negotiation and signing. 
  • Provide project management for active transactions, including timelines, workplans, and status reporting across a portfolio of concurrent deals. 
  • Prepare memos, presentations, and other materials for Executive Leadership and Board discussions. 
  • Execute deals using the team’s standard templates and playbooks, and suggest improvements as gaps come up. 
  • As needed, conduct market and benchmarking research to support specific transactions. 
  • Contribute to special projects with Federation-wide impact.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or a related field. 
  • 3 - 7 years of experience in corporate development, investment banking, private equity, transaction advisory, strategy consulting, or finance/corporate finance. 
  • Hands-on experience executing transactions, including financial modeling and due diligence. 
  • Strong analytical, valuation, and corporate finance skills. 
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence stakeholders without direct authority. 
  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication, with the ability to turn complex analysis into executive-ready materials. 
  • Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines across concurrent workstreams. 
  • Able and willing to work non-traditional hours as needed.
  • Able and willing to travel up to 30% of the year.
  • Must be able to connect "micro" details to the "macro" vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook).
  • Able to work from our National Training Center in Fayetteville, GA.

Desired Qualifications

  • MBA, CFA, or progress toward one. 
  • Experience in sports, media, nonprofit, or membership organizations.

U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.
U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.
Position Description
The Corporate Development team leads U.S. Soccer’s inorganic growth initiatives, advancing strategic priorities and creating long-term value for the Federation. Our work includes mergers and acquisitions, joint ventures, strategic investments / partnerships, integration planning and real estate development. We partner with teams across U.S. Soccer, including Finance, Strategy, and Legal to deliver on our projects.
The Senior Director, Corporate Development will lead due diligence, deal negotiations, structuring, and manage internal and Board approvals for potential mergers, acquisitions, strategic partnerships, and joint ventures, with a particular focus on US Soccer’s player pathway and regional/local model strategy. This leader will own a portfolio of transactions end to end, collaborating with cross functional teams at US Soccer and external stakeholders including State Associations and other regional and local soccer organizations.
Primary Responsibilities
- Develop and maintain the transaction strategy and pipeline for regional/local model strategy, aligned with the U.S. Soccer’s strategic priorities. - Lead deal structuring and negotiation of key terms across multiple concurrent transactions, working closely with Legal and outside counsel through definitive documentation and close. - Direct financial, commercial, people, operational, and legal due diligence, coordinating internal workstreams and external advisors. - Oversee financial models and analyses, including transaction economics, funding, pro formas, and scenario analyses. - Build repeatable templates, playbooks, and trackers that standardize the process across similar transactions. - Identify, quantify, and mitigate transaction risks. - Hand off diligence findings and commitments to the integration team to support integration planning. - Direct and mentor deal team members within the Corporate Development team. - Lead special projects with Federation-wide impact as needed. - Prepare strategic discussion materials for Executive Leadership and the Board decision making.
Requirements
Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or a related field. - 7+ years of experience in corporate development, investment banking, private equity, strategy consulting, or finance/corporate finance, including significant experience leading transactions from origination through close. - Demonstrated success negotiating and structuring M&A, joint venture, or strategic partnership transactions. - Proven ability to lead teams and manage multiple complex workstreams and external advisors at once. - Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the judgment to navigate sensitive negotiations and stakeholder relationships. - General knowledge of soccer. - Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments. - Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission. - Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook). - Able and willing to work non-traditional hours as needed. - Able and willing to travel up to 30% of the year.
Desired Qualifications
- MBA, CFA, or other advanced degree. - Experience in sports, nonprofit, membership, or federated organizations, or with multi-site roll-up transactions. - Familiarity with the U.S. youth and amateur soccer landscape. - Experience negotiating with member-led or volunteer-governed boards.
U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.
U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

This includes leading the regional delivery of R90+ and ensuring the program is effectively connected to the wider referee development pathway.The Regional Refereeing Lead builds strong relationships across the region, supports State Referee Committees and local organizations in implementing national priorities, and brings regional insight directly into how refereeing programs are designed, refined, and delivered.The position coordinates referees, coaches, and development activity across matches, coaching touchpoints, assessments, and regional events, ensuring a consistent and practical approach to referee development.The Regional Refereeing Lead also contributes to talent identification and progression by providing performance insight, observations, and recommendations to support national decision-making.Working closely with national refereeing staff and fellow Regional Refereeing Leads, the position ensures regional delivery aligns with national standards while helping shape how national programs evolve. The role brings a clear view of regional activity, emerging talent, development needs, challenges, and opportunities into national planning and decision-making.  As U.S. Soccer’s refereeing voice in the West, the Regional Refereeing Lead must be an exceptional communicator. This person explains national direction clearly in writing and in person, presents confidently to audiences ranging from volunteer referees to state leadership, and can deliver difficult or unpopular decisions while keeping the trust and credibility of the people affected.Primary ResponsibilitiesBuild and maintain strong working relationships with State Referee Committees, local referee organizations, competition partners, and regional programs to support alignment with U.S. Soccer refereeing strategy.Serve as a key U.S. Soccer refereeing development contact for State Referee Committees across the West, maintaining regular engagement, understanding regional needs, and supporting implementation of national initiatives.Support the regional delivery of national programs across referee education, coaching, evaluation, referee safety, talent identification, and development.Gather structured feedback from regional stakeholders and work with national staff to shape the design, refinement, and rollout of refereeing programs, bringing a regional perspective into national planning rather than reporting on delivery.Collaborate with peer Regional Refereeing Leads to share effective practice, align delivery and coaching standards, coordinate cross-regional opportunities such as shared events and referee exchanges, and ensure a consistent national experience for referees and coaches.Coordinate regional referee development activities across matches, coaching touchpoints, assessments, and events to support continuous development.Lead the regional delivery of R90+, ensuring alignment with national standards, structure, and expectations.Support the ongoing development of R90+ participants through coaching, development planning, match opportunities, regional events, and performance tracking.Lead and coordinate the regional coaching network, working with stakeholders to allocate coaches, oversee delivery, and maintain consistent coaching standards.Coordinate and guide the assignment of referees to appropriate development matches, events, and opportunities, aligning activity to referee readiness and program objectives.Build relationships with regional competitions and events to create appropriate development, observation, coaching, and talent identification opportunities for referees.Ensure regional referee development activity is accurately captured within U.S. Soccer’s referee intelligence platforms, supporting consistent tracking, accurate data, and effective use of insights.Identify and monitor referees with potential for progression, providing performance data, observations, and recommendations to support national selection and advancement decisions.Maintain a clear view of referee and coach development across the West and provide regular insight to national staff on regional activity, emerging talent, development needs, risks, and opportunities.Act as the primary voice of U.S. Soccer refereeing in the West, communicating national programs, priorities, and decisions through written updates, presentations, and direct conversations, including explaining difficult or unpopular decisions in a way that maintains trust and credibility.Work with operational teams to support the effective planning and delivery of regional events and development activity.

job.title: Director, Prospect Development & Strategy
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description

  

Reporting to the Senior Director, Advancement Services, the Director, Prospect Development & Strategy will build and lead U.S. Soccer's prospect development and fundraising strategy capabilities, establishing the frameworks, practices, and fundraising discipline needed to support an Advancement program raising $70M+ annually and scaling toward $100M.


Serving as a strategic partner to Advancement leadership and frontline fundraisers, the Director will bring deep fundraising expertise and relationship-management practices to prospect identification, portfolio strategy, pipeline development, and moves management. With particular emphasis on principal, transformational, and complex philanthropic opportunities, this role will help fundraisers identify the strongest pathways to advance donor relationships and drive philanthropic growth.


In partnership with the Senior Director, Advancement Services, the Director will lead the development of prospect and portfolio management capabilities within Salesforce, embed U.S. Soccer's frontline fundraising methodology into daily practices, and oversee the growth and effectiveness of the prospect development function.


We’d love to learn more about you—please include a brief cover letter sharing why you’re excited about this role and what you’d bring to the team. 


Primary Responsibilities

  • Develop and lead a comprehensive prospect development strategy aligned with U.S. Soccer's fundraising priorities, campaign objectives, and long-term philanthropic growth.
  • Build and scale prospect development capabilities by establishing the strategic roadmap, operating framework, performance measures, and resources needed to support a growing Advancement program.
  • Partner across Major Gifts, Principal Gifts, Annual Fund, Institutional Giving, Stewardship, and Advancement leadership to align prospect development strategy, fundraising priorities, pipeline growth, and relationship-management practices.
  • Partner with fundraising leadership to develop and advance strategies for principal, transformational, stalled, and complex philanthropic opportunities, identifying relationship dynamics, barriers, strategic connections, and next actions.
  • Serve as a strategic thought partner to leadership and frontline fundraisers on relationship and account strategy, cultivation, solicitation planning, and opportunity progression.
  • Lead the design and implementation of a comprehensive moves-management program, establishing clear definitions, business rules, and milestones for prospect qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and ongoing relationship management.
  • Establish portfolio and pipeline management standards, including qualification criteria, portfolio composition, assignment and reassignment practices, capacity expectations, opportunity stages, aging standards, and next-action requirements. Lead regular portfolio and pipeline reviews that strengthen accountability and advance donor relationships.
  • Establish strategic priorities and expectations for prospect identification, research, screening, and qualification, ensuring research produces timely, actionable intelligence that supports fundraising strategy and leadership-level giving.
  • Partner with fundraisers and leadership to translate prospect intelligence into recommendations for prioritization, relationship strategy, assignments, and next actions that advance qualified prospects through the pipeline.
  • Lead, supervise, mentor, and develop the Manager, Prospect Research & Management, overseeing the effectiveness and growth of the research function and assessing future staffing and resource needs.
  • Lead the implementation and adoption of U.S. Soccer's frontline fundraising methodology, including Plus Delta, integrating relationship-management practices into fundraising strategy, coaching, portfolio management, and pipeline reviews.
  • Help lead the definition of business requirements for prospect development and management capabilities within Salesforce, including functional requirements, workflows, data standards, and processes that support frontline fundraising and drive adoption.
  • Monitor portfolio and pipeline health, prospect movement, qualification effectiveness, and adoption of established practices to identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Support the strategic priorities and growth of the Advancement department and perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in prospect development, major/principal gift fundraising strategy, advancement leadership, relationship/account management, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience building, transforming, or significantly scaling a prospect development, fundraising strategy, or relationship-management function.
  • Deep understanding of major and principal gift fundraising best practices, including qualification, portfolio and pipeline management, moves management, cultivation, solicitation, and relationship strategy.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and advising on strategies for principal, transformational, and complex philanthropic opportunities, including high-capacity donor engagement, relationship mapping, and solicitation planning.
  • Proven ability to serve as a strategic partner to senior Advancement leadership and frontline fundraisers, translating research, data, and relationship intelligence into actionable fundraising strategies and coaching fundraisers on opportunity progression.
  • Experience designing and implementing portfolio, pipeline, qualification, and moves-management frameworks within a complex fundraising or relationship-driven organization.
  • Experience translating fundraising strategy and business requirements into CRM processes and functionality; experience implementing prospect management capabilities in Salesforce or a comparable CRM strongly preferred.
  • Experience implementing fundraising methodologies or significant changes in frontline practices and driving adoption; familiarity with Plus Delta or similar relationship-based fundraising methodologies preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience hiring, supervising, coaching, and developing professional staff, including building team capabilities and establishing clear performance expectations.
  • Exceptional strategic thinking, facilitation, coaching, communication, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence senior leadership and work effectively across functions.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead organizational change, establish new processes and operating practices, and balance strategic planning with hands-on implementation.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).

Desired Qualifications

  • General knowledge of soccer preferred.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Director of Campus Security is responsible for developing, implementing, and managing all security operations at the Arthur M. Blank U.S. Soccer National Training Center. This role ensures the safety of athletes, staff, visitors, and assets while maintaining a secure and professional environment.


This position plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety and security of the National Training Center, supporting the mission and values of the United States Soccer Federation.


Primary Responsibilities

  

Security Operations & Risk Management

  • Develop and enforce comprehensive security policies, procedures, and protocols for the National Training Center.
  • Oversee access control, surveillance systems, and perimeter security measures.
  • Conduct security risk assessments and implement mitigation strategies.
  • Lead emergency preparedness planning, including fire safety, severe weather response, and active threat protocols.
  • Coordinate security for high-profile events, training camps, and international team visits.

Personnel Management & Training

  • Supervise and manage on-site security personnel, including third-party security contractors.
  • Develop and conduct regular security training programs for staff, athletes, and security personnel.
  • Establish a security culture by promoting awareness and best practices throughout the campus.

Incident Response & Investigations

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for security incidents, coordinating response efforts with local law enforcement, emergency services, and USSF leadership.
  • Investigate security breaches, threats, and other incidents, ensuring timely reporting and resolution.
  • Maintain detailed records of incidents and prepare reports for senior leadership.

Collaboration & Compliance

  • Work closely with the Vice President of Security, and Director of Security Operations to align security strategies with organizational goals.
  • Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local security regulations, as well as USSF policies.
  • Collaborate with facilities management, IT security, and event operations to ensure a holistic security approach.

Technology & Infrastructure Security

  • Oversee the maintenance and upgrades of security technology, including surveillance cameras, alarm systems, and access control systems.
  • Coordinate cybersecurity measures with IT teams to protect sensitive information and operational systems.

Work Environment & Travel

  • Based at the National Training Center in Fayetteville, GA with limited travel for security assessments, training, and USSF events.
  • On-call availability for emergency situations, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed.  

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice, Security Management, Homeland Security, or a related field (Master’s preferred).
  • 7-10 years of experience in security management, law enforcement, or military service, preferably in a campus, sports facility, or corporate environment.
  • Strong leadership and crisis management skills with experience handling large-scale security operations.
  • Knowledge of emergency response planning, risk assessment, and investigative procedures.
  • Familiarity with security technologies, including surveillance systems, access control, and cybersecurity protocols.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across departments.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain security clearances and certifications as required.
  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).

Desired Qualifications

  • Law Enforcement Officers Safety Act (LEOSA) Certification
  • Certified Protection Professional (CPP)
  • Physical Security Professional (PSP)
  • Certified Homeland Protection Professional (CHPP)
  • First Aid/CPR/AED Certification
  • General knowledge of soccer

This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.
U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.
Position Description
The Director of Campus Security is responsible for developing, implementing, and managing all security operations at the Arthur M. Blank U.S. Soccer National Training Center. This role ensures the safety of athletes, staff, visitors, and assets while maintaining a secure and professional environment.
This position plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety and security of the National Training Center, supporting the mission and values of the United States Soccer Federation.
Primary Responsibilities
Security Operations & Risk Management
- Develop and enforce comprehensive security policies, procedures, and protocols for the National Training Center. - Oversee access control, surveillance systems, and perimeter security measures. - Conduct security risk assessments and implement mitigation strategies. - Lead emergency preparedness planning, including fire safety, severe weather response, and active threat protocols. - Coordinate security for high-profile events, training camps, and international team visits.
Personnel Management & Training
- Supervise and manage on-site security personnel, including third-party security contractors. - Develop and conduct regular security training programs for staff, athletes, and security personnel. - Establish a security culture by promoting awareness and best practices throughout the campus.
Incident Response & Investigations
- Serve as the primary point of contact for security incidents, coordinating response efforts with local law enforcement, emergency services, and USSF leadership. - Investigate security breaches, threats, and other incidents, ensuring timely reporting and resolution. - Maintain detailed records of incidents and prepare reports for senior leadership.
Collaboration & Compliance
- Work closely with the Vice President of Security, and Director of Security Operations to align security strategies with organizational goals. - Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local security regulations, as well as USSF policies. - Collaborate with facilities management, IT security, and event operations to ensure a holistic security approach.
Technology & Infrastructure Security
- Oversee the maintenance and upgrades of security technology, including surveillance cameras, alarm systems, and access control systems. - Coordinate cybersecurity measures with IT teams to protect sensitive information and operational systems.
Work Environment & Travel
- Based at the National Training Center in Fayetteville, GA with limited travel for security assessments, training, and USSF events. - On-call availability for emergency situations, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed.
Requirements
Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice, Security Management, Homeland Security, or a related field (Master’s preferred). - 7-10 years of experience in security management, law enforcement, or military service, preferably in a campus, sports facility, or corporate environment. - Strong leadership and crisis management skills with experience handling large-scale security operations. - Knowledge of emergency response planning, risk assessment, and investigative procedures. - Familiarity with security technologies, including surveillance systems, access control, and cybersecurity protocols. - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across departments. - Ability to obtain and maintain security clearances and certifications as required. - General knowledge of soccer. - Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments. - Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission. - Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).
Desired Qualifications
- Law Enforcement Officers Safety Act (LEOSA) Certification - Certified Protection Professional (CPP) - Physical Security Professional (PSP) - Certified Homeland Protection Professional (CHPP) - First Aid/CPR/AED Certification - General knowledge of soccer
U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.
U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.
